w: Founded December 4, 1786 - the feast of Saint Barbara - by Padre Fermin Lasuen, the tenth of 21 California missions, earning the nickname Queen of the Missions. Chumash-Barbareno people were converted and put to forced labor building it. The mission gave its name to the city and county of Santa Barbara.
s: Queen of the Missions, founded 1786 by Padre Lasuen
_facts: Founded Dec 4, 1786 by Padre Fermin Lasuen, the tenth of 21 California missions
Called the Queen of the Missions
Chumash-Barbareno people converted and put to forced labor under the mission system
Namesake of the city and county of Santa Barbara

w: Founded in 1941 in downtown Santa Barbara, the museum holds permanent collections spanning Asian, American and European art across four thousand years, from antiquity to the present, alongside rotating special exhibitions.
s: Downtown museum spanning 4,000 years of art since 1941
_facts: Founded 1941
Downtown Santa Barbara location
Permanent collection covers Asian, American and European art across 4,000 years

w: The Montecito estate of Madame Ganna Walska, Lotusland covers 37 acres and holds 3,500 plant species in a non-profit botanical garden. Santa Barbara County allows entry only by reservation, under a conditional use permit, keeping the grounds and their varied plant collections deliberately hard to reach.
_facts: Historic estate of Madame Ganna Walska
37 acres (15 ha), home to 3,500 plant species
Visits restricted to reservation only under a county conditional use permit

n: Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History
w: Its Mission Canyon campus sits along Mission Creek in the Upper Eastside; its ocean-focused Sea Center occupies Stearns Wharf. Together they draw about 230,000 visitors a year to halls on Chumash history and native wildlife, plus what the museum calls the Central Coast's only full-dome planetarium.
s: Mission Canyon halls plus a Stearns Wharf Sea Center
_facts: Two campuses: Mission Canyon (Upper Eastside) and the Sea Center on Stearns Wharf
About 230,000 visitors a year, split evenly between campuses
Houses the Palmer Observatory and a Chumash history exhibit
Claims the only full-dome planetarium on the Central Coast

w: Built in the Mission Revival and Spanish Colonial Revival styles, the Arlington is Santa Barbara's largest movie theater and main performing arts venue, seating 2,010. Beyond regular screenings, it anchors the annual Santa Barbara International Film Festival.
_facts: Combines Mission Revival and Spanish Colonial Revival architecture
Largest movie theater in the city, seats 2,010
Hosts the Santa Barbara International Film Festival

w: Roscoe 'Fatty' Arbuckle, Charlie Chaplin and friends built this Coast Village Road hotel in 1928 as an escape from Hollywood, 2.5 blocks from Butterfly Beach. Chaplin's films fill its library, his image is etched into the glass doors, and the 1936 song 'There's a Small Hotel' is said to have drawn on the inn.
s: Built in 1928 by Charlie Chaplin and Fatty Arbuckle
_facts: Built 1928 by Roscoe 'Fatty' Arbuckle, Charlie Chaplin and friends
2.5 blocks from Butterfly Beach on Coast Village Road
Holds a complete library of Chaplin's films, his image etched into the doors
Said to have inspired the 1936 Rodgers and Hart song 'There's a Small Hotel'

w: Set in Mission Canyon beside Mission Santa Barbara, the 78-acre garden displays over 1,000 species of rare and indigenous California plants across 5.7 miles of trails. Mission Creek runs through it, crossed by a rock dam built in 1806 by Canalino laborers under the Spanish mission padres.
s: 1,000+ native species and a rock dam built in 1806
_facts: 78 acres (32 ha), over 1,000 species of rare and indigenous plants
5.7 miles of hiking trails
Mission Creek runs through it, crossed by an 1806 rock dam built by Canalino laborers

w: Built between 1926 and 1929, the courthouse still houses six Superior Court rooms, the Hall of Records and the Mural Room. Architect Charles Willard Moore called it the grandest Spanish Colonial Revival structure ever built; it's now a National Historic Landmark and a popular wedding venue.
s: 1929 Spanish Colonial Revival courthouse, still in use
_facts: Built 1926-1929, Spanish Colonial Revival style
Still houses six Superior Court rooms, the Hall of Records and the Mural Room
National Historic Landmark since 2005
Called by architect Charles Willard Moore the grandest Spanish Colonial Revival structure ever built

w: Jose Lobero founded the original opera house in 1873; the present building, designed by George Washington Smith and Lutah Maria Riggs in Spanish Colonial Revival style, replaced it in 1924. Gable, Stravinsky, Rachmaninoff and Bing Crosby all appeared here, now California's oldest continuously operating theatre.
_facts: Founded 1873 by Jose Lobero; California's oldest continuously operating theater
Current 1924 building designed by George Washington Smith and Lutah Maria Riggs
Performers have included Clark Gable, Stravinsky, Rachmaninoff and Bing Crosby
Named in 2023 among Architectural Digest's eleven most beautiful theaters

w: Built on the grounds of the old Child Estate and opened in August 1963, the 30-acre zoo keeps more than 500 animals, including capybaras and California condors, and was long known for a giraffe with a crooked neck. A narrow-gauge Zoo Train, pulled by C.P. Huntington locomotives, still runs through the grounds.
s: 30-acre zoo on a former estate, opened 1963
_facts: Opened August 1963 on the former Child Estate
